content.text:
I've built the part as a dog-bone link and exported it to `submission.step`. On the four-view comparison with `composite.png` it scored 0.864 out of 1; the tool counts about 0.95 or more as a match, so this is close but not exact.

**What the part is:** a flat plate 102 long (along Y) × 32 tall (along Z) × 5 thick (along X), in mm. It is a straight bar 26 wide, with a round lobe of radius 16 at each end. Each lobe has a through-hole of diameter 9 at its center.

**How I got there:** I tried several orientations. Lying flat in XY scored about 0.44. Tilting the plate 45° and 70° about Y raised it to 0.54 and 0.76. Standing it upright in the YZ plane jumped the score to 0.86. I then adjusted the lobe size, hole size and hole positions. Those changes stayed between 0.84 and 0.86 and none beat the first upright version, so that is the one I exported.

**Checks:** the exported STEP was read back and is one valid solid, with the same volume and size as the model.

The part was made with a script, not native editable FreeCAD features. That doesn't affect the STEP file.
